description: A `run:` step pipes the output of `curl` or `wget` directly into a shell interpreter. This is the "curl | bash" install pattern — if the remote server is compromised or the URL is hijacked, an attacker can execute arbitrary code in your CI runner. Consider downloading the file first, verifying its checksum or signature, and then executing it.

description: Using variable interpolation `${{...}}` with `github` context data in a `run:` step could allow an attacker to inject their own code into the runner. This would allow them to steal secrets and code. `github` context data can have arbitrary user input and should be treated as untrusted. Instead, use an intermediate environment variable with `env:` to store the data and use the environment variable in the `run:` script. Be sure to use double-quotes the environment variable, like this: "$ENVVAR".

description: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using an object-relational mapper (ORM) such as Sequelize which will protect your queries.

description: Possibility of prototype polluting function detected. By adding or modifying attributes of an object prototype, it is possible to create attributes that exist on every object, or replace critical attributes with malicious ones. This can be problematic if the software depends on existence or non-existence of certain attributes, or uses pre-defined attributes of object prototype (such as hasOwnProperty, toString or valueOf). Possible mitigations might be: freezing the object prototype, using an object without prototypes (via Object.create(null) ), blocking modifications of attributes that resolve to object prototype, using Map instead of object.

description:
In changePassword, the current-password check is guarded by `if (currentPassword && ...)`. An empty or missing currentPassword makes the guard falsy, skipping verification entirely and allowing password change with only a valid auth token.
Scout rationale and verification strategy: Line 39: `if (currentPassword && security.hash(currentPassword) !== loggedInUser.data.password)` — when currentPassword is '' or undefined the short-circuit skips the check. Lines 44-51 then update the password unconditionally. Verification: send a valid Bearer token with query params current= (empty) and new=attackerpass; expect 200 and subsequent login with attackerpass.

description:

Scout rationale and verification strategy: Line 51: `await user.update({ password: newPasswordInString })` — newPasswordInString is just newPassword?.toString() with no hash call. Compare with line 39 which uses security.hash() for comparison, confirming the stored format should be hashed. resetPassword.ts:44 has the same pattern. Verification: change password via API, then query the DB or attempt login with the raw new password; expect success confirming plaintext storage.
